title: The version check raises the version and pushes it
check-bump raises a missing version bump itself (fixing mode)
body:
Part of epic gsv-1fc3 (unit 2 of plan git-dev-aef7; delivers into plan/git-dev-aef7). Owner decisions not to reopen: in the pull request mode a change to configured files without a higher version is fixed by the check; any bump the author already made stands (minor/major stay a person's decision); the automatic bump is always a patch. This issue is the LOCAL half only: no push, no token, no network. Pushing is issue 2 of the epic.

## Current code (re-validated 2026-11-28 against git-semver 0.1.1)
- `cmd_check_bump` (git-semver line 570): reads base from --base / CICD_BASE (required), head from --head / CICD_HEAD / HEAD; `verify_commit` both; `get_changed_files_between(base, head)`; iterates `[(None, config)] + get_subdirectories(config).items()` calling `check_bump_component` (line 523), which returns (ok, lines). Docstring says 'Read-only and local ... writes nothing' — must be updated.
- `check_bump_component` decides: no `files` -> skipped; no configured file and no version-file change -> pass; head version > base (or base missing/malformed) -> pass 'version raised'; otherwise FAIL with reason (missing / malformed / still X / went down to X) and fix line `git-semver bump patch --no-push [--subdir <d>]`.
- `bump_component(config, subdir, bump_type, description)` (line 413): reads VERSION, uses the higher of VERSION or latest tag as baseline (`get_latest_tag_version`), writes version file, `apply_updates(effective.get('updates', {}), new_version)`, `update_changelog(...)` when `parse_changelog_config` enables it. Returns (subdir, old, new, tag).
- `cmd_bump` (line 600) commits with `git add -A` + `git commit -m 'chore: bump version to <tag>'`.
- Parser: `check-bump` subparser at line 862 with --base, --head.
- `templates/config.schema` documents top-level keys (`bump_on` etc.); config keys are listed in the `KNOWN`-style tuple at git-semver line 33 (`version_file, files, updates, changelog, install, bump_on`).

## Behaviour to implement
1. Fixing mode. For the root and every subdirectory component, when check_bump_component would FAIL because the version is equal to the base's (the 'is still X' case), raise it by a patch with `bump_component(config, subdir, 'patch')` (so `updates` and the changelog entry are applied exactly as `bump` does), then make ONE commit for all raised components. Commit message names every raised component with old -> new, e.g. `chore: bump version (root 0.1.1 -> 0.1.2, backend 0.3.0 -> 0.3.1)`; decision: subject prefixed `chore: bump version` to match existing bump commits. Stage only the files the bump wrote (version files, `updates` targets, changelog files), not `git add -A`, so unrelated working-tree changes in CI are never committed.
2. A component whose version is already higher than base by any amount: untouched, passes as today.
3. A version that went DOWN, is malformed, or a version file that is missing at head: an error exactly as today (FAIL with the existing message); never fixed. If any component is in this state, no commit is made at all (decision: fail closed rather than commit a partial fix).
4. Nothing to fix: no commit; output and exit code as today.
5. The fix is made on top of `head`. Decision: fixing mode requires `head` to be the commit currently checked out (`git rev-parse HEAD` equals the resolved head); otherwise it is a SemverError naming both commits (git-cicd's open workflow checks out `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` detached, so in CI they match). Bump baseline: the base's version is what must be exceeded; bump_component's tag-ahead baseline rule stays, and the resulting version must be > base's version (assert/err if not).
6. Exit code / output when a fix commit was made locally (this issue, before push exists): print each raised component and the new commit SHA, and return 1 (the commit under test still lacked the bump; issue 2 refines the messages when it pushes). The existing `fix:` hint lines still print.
7. Mode selection. New config key `push_bump` (boolean) — decision: one key for 'fix and push' because the doc describes a single documented setting that turns the behaviour off (check only, as today); a fix without a push is only reachable locally. Default: true when `bump_on` is `pull_request`, false otherwise. Arguments `--fix` / `--no-fix` (mutually exclusive) on `check-bump` override the config either way. Add `push_bump` to the known-keys tuple (line 33) and to `templates/config.schema` with a description ('With bump_on pull_request: check-bump raises a missing version by a patch and pushes it to the pull request branch (default true); false = check only'). Update `cmd_check_bump` docstring and the parser help.
8. Root-level `files` absent but subdir components present must keep working (components loop unchanged).

## Out of scope
Pushing, tokens, branch safety (issue 2); README/AGENTS docs and the VERSION bump (issue 3). `release bump`, `release publish`, bump-on-merge default, `install.sh`, `templates/github/workflows/version-bump.yml` do not change. No vendor-protected file touched.

## Tests (extend tests/test_check_bump.py, which builds real git repos with the `repo` fixture and `subprocess`)
- configured file changed, version equal: one new commit; VERSION is base patch+1; an `updates` target rewritten; CHANGELOG entry added; commit message lists root old -> new; exit 1.
- root + subdir both needing a bump: exactly one commit naming both.
- root raised by minor already, subdir needing a bump: only subdir raised.
- any bump already made (patch, minor, major): no commit, exit 0.
- version went down / malformed / missing: no commit, FAIL message as today, exit 1; with a second component that would be fixable still no commit.
- nothing changed: no commit, exit 0.
- --no-fix with bump_on pull_request: no commit, today's output; --fix with bump_on merge: commit made; config push_bump false: no commit.
- head \!= checked-out HEAD in fixing mode: SemverError.
- unrelated untracked/modified file in the worktree is not in the fix commit.
- existing subprocess test class (line ~287) gains a fixing-mode case so the CLI path is covered.

## Acceptance criteria
- All cases above pass; coverage for git-semver and release stays >= 99% (`.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check --setup`).
- `push_bump` documented in templates/config.schema; --fix/--no-fix in `git-semver check-bump --help`.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7` reports nothing.

title: check-bump pushes its fix commit to the pull request branch with CICD_WRITE_TOKEN, safely
body:
Part of epic gsv-1fc3 (unit 2 of plan git-dev-aef7; delivers into plan/git-dev-aef7). Depends on gsv-1fc3.1 (fixing mode: check-bump makes one local patch-bump commit on top of the checked-out head; config key `push_bump`, args --fix/--no-fix). This issue adds the push.

## Owner decisions (do not reopen)
- Pushed by default in the pull request mode; `push_bump: false` / --no-fix turns it off (check only, as today).
- The push uses `CICD_WRITE_TOKEN` (a push made with the workflow's own GITHUB_TOKEN starts no workflow, leaving the pushed commit unchecked). git-cicd gives a job a secret only when the job declares it (`"secrets": ["CICD_WRITE_TOKEN"]`, unit 1 of the plan), so in CI it is present only for a job that asked. Without it (fork, no secret, no declaration) nothing is pushed and the check fails naming the command, as today.
- Only to the pull request's source branch, only when that branch is in this repository, never to the release branch.
- The token value is never printed. No test reads a token from the environment.

## Decision: git-semver owns the push
`check-bump` lives in git-semver and the version-check job runs `git-semver check-bump` directly (.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json job `version-check`); `release` (whose tokens are documented in its module docstring, lines 55-56: GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN) is not on that path. So the push code goes in `git-semver` next to `cmd_check_bump` (line 570). `release` is unchanged.

## Inputs
git-cicd's variables, set by `script_env` in .vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd (~line 850): `CICD_SOURCE_BRANCH`, `CICD_TARGET_BRANCH`, `CICD_BASE`, `CICD_HEAD`. Add `--source-branch` and `--target-branch` arguments to the `check-bump` parser (line 862); arguments win over the variables, as --base/--head already do. Remote: `origin` (decision: the same remote `release` and `cmd_bump` push to).

## Decision procedure after a fix commit (each branch returns non-zero; only the first is a push)
Refuse WITHOUT pushing, printing a one-line reason plus today's `fix:` line (`git-semver bump patch --no-push [--subdir d]`), when:
1. no `CICD_WRITE_TOKEN` (or empty) -> reason 'no CICD_WRITE_TOKEN: declare it on the version check job';
2. source branch unknown (neither arg nor CICD_SOURCE_BRANCH);
3. source branch == target branch;
4. source branch is a release branch. Decision: git-semver has no release-branch config, so 'release branch' = the target branch, `main`, and `master` (the branches the git-cicd release job and version-bump.yml release from); recorded because the doc leaves it undefined;
5. source branch does not exist on origin (`git ls-remote --heads origin refs/heads/<source>` empty) — this is also the fork case, since a fork's branch is not on this repository's remote;
6. source branch on origin is not at the commit under test (remote SHA != resolved head, i.e. CICD_HEAD) -> 'branch moved on from <head>'.
Otherwise push `HEAD:refs/heads/<source>` to origin with no force (a non-fast-forward is also rejected by git). On push failure: print git's stderr with the token redacted, fail as in the refusals.

## Token handling
Give the token to git for that one push only, never on the command line, in .git/config, or in any message. Decision: pass it through the environment as config — `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=http.https://github.com/.extraheader` with an EMPTY value (resets the extraheader that actions/checkout@v4 persists with GITHUB_TOKEN; git docs: an empty value resets the list), `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1` same key with `AUTHORIZATION: basic <base64('x-access-token:'+token)>`. Requires git >= 2.31 (runner and dev have 2.43). Implementer re-checks the header form against how actions/checkout@v4 writes it (`.github/workflows/git-cicd-open.yml` line ~88 checks out `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` with default persist-credentials). Any text git returns is passed through a redactor that replaces the token and its base64 form with `***` before printing.

## Exit and messages when pushed
Exit 1 (decision: non-zero so the commit that lacked the bump gets no pass from the verdict; the doc only requires 'not a pass'), printing: the components raised (old -> new), the pushed SHA and branch, and 'the pushed commit <sha> starts its own run; wait for that one'.
When pushing is turned off (push_bump false / --no-fix): no commit, today's behaviour (from gsv-1fc3.1).

## Tests (tests/test_check_bump.py; replace `git push` / `git ls-remote` at the boundary the existing tests use — see tests/test_tag_on_merge.py ~line 74 which intercepts `('git','push')` commands, and tests/test_bump_and_release.py `set_response(['git','push'], ...)`)
Tests set CICD_WRITE_TOKEN themselves with a fake value via monkeypatch (never read the real one). One test per branch: no token; no source branch; source==target; source is main/master/target; branch absent on origin (fork); branch moved on; push succeeds (asserts argv is exactly push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<src> with no token in argv, env carries the GIT_CONFIG_* entries, exit 1, wait-for message); push fails (redacted stderr, exit 1); args override CICD_ vars. A test asserts the fake token and its base64 never appear in captured stdout/stderr, in the commit message, or in `git config --list` of the repo afterwards. A subprocess-level test (pattern at test_check_bump.py ~line 287) covers one pushed path with a local bare repo as origin so the real git push runs (token header harmless against a file remote).

## Acceptance criteria
- Change without a bump: one patch commit with updates+changelog, pushed to the source branch with the write token, run exits non-zero with the wait-for-the-new-run message.
- Bump already made: no commit, no push, exit 0.
- No token, fork, or pushing turned off: nothing pushed, check fails naming the command.
- Refuses (with a reason) the target branch, a release branch, a branch not on origin, a branch that moved on.
- Token in no output, commit or leftover git config (asserted on captured output).
- Coverage >= 99% for git-semver and release; `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7` reports nothing.
Out of scope: docs/VERSION (gsv-1fc3.3), this repo's own git-cicd job declaration (adoption unit), any change in git-cicd or git-vendored.

title: Test suite strips real tokens; docs describe the pushed bump; raise VERSION
body:
Part of epic gsv-1fc3 (unit 2 of plan git-dev-aef7; delivers into plan/git-dev-aef7). Docs part depends on gsv-1fc3.1 (fixing mode, config key `push_bump`, --fix/--no-fix) and gsv-1fc3.2 (push with CICD_WRITE_TOKEN, refusals). The token guard can land first.

## 1. Token guard (why: in mangimangi/git-vendored a test that picked up the repository's real token printed a shortened form of it in a public log)
Five names: CICD_WRITE_TOKEN, CICD_READ_TOKEN, VENDOR_PAT, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN.
- pytest: one autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py (currently has only `tmp_repo`, `make_config`, `make_version_file` fixtures and the extensionless imports of git-semver/release) that `monkeypatch.delenv(name, raising=False)` for all five before every test. Existing per-test delenv loops (e.g. tests/test_check_bump.py line ~50 and ~150) may stay or be simplified; tests that need a fake token keep setting it with monkeypatch after the guard.
- bats: tests/bats/helpers.bash `sandbox()` already unsets `GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN VENDOR_PAT` among others; add CICD_WRITE_TOKEN and CICD_READ_TOKEN there (the one place for bats).
- A test fails if the guard is removed. Decision (a test that only asserts the variables are absent would still pass on a runner that has none): pytest — a test runs `python -m pytest` in a subprocess on a small probe test file with all five exported to real-looking fake values and the repo's conftest active (e.g. probe placed under tests/ via `--rootdir`/`-p` or a tmp copy that imports the guard), and asserts the probe saw none of them; bats — a test exports all five with fake values, calls `sandbox`, and asserts each is unset.
- The whole suite passes with real-looking values exported for all five outside it (e.g. `CICD_WRITE_TOKEN=ghp_xxx... ci/test.sh`); state this in the PR.

## 2. Docs
README.md (sections: `### git-semver check-bump [--base <rev>] [--head <rev>]` ~line 166, `### Keys` ~line 243, `### Bumping in the pull request (bump_on: pull_request)` ~line 404, `### Releasing with git-cicd` ~line 424, `### Authentication` ~line 507). Describe the pull request mode as it now is: what gets pushed (one patch commit on the source branch raising each component whose configured files changed without a higher version, with updates and changelog), when nothing is (a bump already made by any amount; push_bump false or --no-fix; no token; fork; refusals: target/release branch, branch not on origin, branch moved on), that the run exits non-zero and the pushed commit's own run is the one to wait for, which token (`CICD_WRITE_TOKEN`) and which permission it needs (contents: write on this repository — fine-grained PAT or app token; a GITHUB_TOKEN push starts no workflow), how to turn pushing off (`"push_bump": false` or `--no-fix`), the new `--fix/--no-fix/--source-branch/--target-branch` arguments, and the git-cicd job declaration (`"secrets": ["CICD_WRITE_TOKEN"]` on the version check job, as git-cicd's README defines it). Update the command heading for the new arguments and the `push_bump` key in Keys.
AGENTS.md: the Releasing section says a change must bump VERSION in the same PR and that version-check 'fails until the version is higher ... and prints that command'; amend to say that with the token declared the check pushes the patch bump itself, and that this repo's job does not declare it yet so the manual `./git-semver bump patch --no-push` still applies here.
Do NOT change this repository's .vendored/configs/git-cicd.json (the declaration is left for the adoption unit, once git-cicd with declarations is installed here) or any generated workflow.

## 3. Version
Raise VERSION (currently 0.1.1) with `./git-semver bump patch --no-push` so CHANGELOG.md gets its entry — decision: patch, matching the doc's 'the pushed bump is a patch' and since the default only changes for bump_on pull_request; do it once, after gsv-1fc3.1 and gsv-1fc3.2, in the same branch, so `git-semver check-bump` passes against origin/main.

## Acceptance criteria
- Guard in tests/conftest.py and tests/bats/helpers.bash for all five names; the guard-removal tests exist and fail when the guard is deleted (verify by temporarily removing it).
- Suite passes with all five exported to real-looking values.
- README and AGENTS.md describe the behaviour above; no git-cicd config or workflow changed.
- VERSION raised with a CHANGELOG entry; `git-semver check-bump --base origin/main` passes.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check --setup` passes with coverage >= 99% for both scripts; the PR into plan/git-dev-aef7 has a passing `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict`; `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7` reports nothing.
